name: Abū Yūsuf Yaʿqūb ibn Isḥāq ibn al-Sikkīt
summary: Kufan lexicographer and grammarian, author of Iṣlāḥ al-manṭiq, the book on the correct forms of words; tutor of al-Mutawakkil's sons, killed at the caliph's order.
bio: Ibn al-Sikkīt learnt from al-Farrāʾ's circle and from the Bedouin, and al-Zubaydī counts him in the third generation of the Kufan lexicographers. His Iṣlāḥ al-manṭiq, 'the setting right of speech', lists words that people got wrong, by their patterns, and was so esteemed that a later scholar said no book of its kind had crossed the bridge of Baghdad.

He taught the sons of the caliph al-Mutawakkil in Samarra. The story of his death is told in several sources: the caliph asked him whether his own sons were dearer to him or al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, and he answered that Qanbar, ʿAlī's servant, was better than the two princes; al-Mutawakkil had him killed. He died in 244/858.
uncertain: The details of his death differ between the sources; some doubt the story.
